Thanks Ellen — helpful. A few concrete patterns we'd recommend for the POC, given your constraints: 

1) Tool/function definitions
- We propose a small manifest format: {id, version, description, input_schema (json-schema), output_schema (json-schema), timeout_ms, retry_policy}.
- Keep tool execution idempotent where possible. Redwood SDK will validate inputs client-side before dispatch.

2) Parallel calls + orchestration
- Client collects top-K candidate tool targets from an internal router (vector search + rules).
- Redwood SDK can fanout parallel tool calls; for safety we recommend an orchestration step in the app layer (Promise.all style / async gather) so partial results can be reconciled by a small coordinator lambda.
- Recommend per-tool timeout windows (e.g., 150ms for vector search, 300ms for external DB) and an overall generation timeout of 700ms.

3) Error handling and fallback
- Hedged retries: on slow responses trigger a secondary (cached) reranker call.
- Fallback model path: if tool outputs fail schema validation, fallback to smaller model to produce a structured suggestion + confidence score, then surface to user.

4) Auth and audit
- For the POC we can start with API-key based service tokens scoped to the Convergent project (fast to stand up) and enable OIDC short-lived tokens in parallel for SSO proof-of-concept.
- Redwood will stream audit events (tool calls + token id) to your audit endpoint or to a secure S3 bucket.

5) Structured output
- Use function-calling style JSON with explicit output_schema. SDK has helpers to coerce and validate.

Hi team — technical recap and concrete recommendations from Redwood infra/product side.

Auth matrix (POC recommendation):
- Phase 1 (fast setup): scoped API keys with per-token project tags. Benefits: fastest to get started, easy to attach billing/quotas.
- Phase 2 (SSO + S2S): Okta OIDC for user-scoped tokens + short-lived service tokens. Where mTLS is policy-required on your side we support it but it needs infra changes on Convergent peering.

Routing policy:
- POC: strict US-east routing (we will pin model and runtime in region).
- Failover: automatic to US-west on capacity fail or degraded latency > 250ms.

SDK snippets (example patterns):
- Node (fanout) — Redwood SDK exposes an async call batcher that returns partial results + per-call metadata. App layer should implement a coordinator to reconcile schema-validated outputs.
- Python — similar pattern; use the SDK's validate() helper to enforce output_schema before commit to reranker.

Tool definitions (recommended minimal):
- id: string (stable),
- version: semver,
- input_schema: JSON-Schema,
- output_schema: JSON-Schema,
- resources: {timeout_ms, mem_limit_mb},
- observability: {emit_trace:true/false}

Reranker guidance:
- Embedding: 512-d, cosine similarity.
- Candidate set: pre-filter to N=50 then rerank top 10 with cross-encoder in Redwood or your side depending on privacy.
- Latency target: add <=200ms for rerank step to meet your 800ms tail.

Audit and compliance:
- We will enable an audit stream for all tool calls (user_id, token_id, tool_id, response_hash). Can deliver to your S3 with server-side encryption or to a secure syslog endpoint.
